rows.capability: Loader, entry point and page-survival model
rows.builder_behavior: ViolentMonkey loader @match whole game origin, @run-at document-idle, @require immutable jsDelivr SHA pin (ce603def, rewritten by pin_release.py); bundle IIFE guarded by window.__tnrBK injects a shadow-DOM FAB on EVERY game page and re-appends itself via MutationObserver if the body is wiped. Build state lives in memory: a navigation reloads the script and loses rows/filemap/last bundle (only idmap and GH settings persist).
rows.forge_behavior: Loader @run-at document-start, same @match, @require pinned to ce603def with @version from forge/package.json. boot(): /forge entry stops the providerless 404, arms the tab (sessionStorage hop counter, MAX_HOPS 2) and redirects to the carrier '/'; on an armed game page it waits for body, mounts one full-screen overlay (.f-host) on top of the live React/Clerk tree, removes old-builder .k-fab/.k-pn nodes only while mounted, and establishes auth. Unarmed pages are untouched. Job state is a write-ahead localStorage journal, so eviction/navigation does not lose the run.

rows.safety_compat_notes: A manifest must be committed to push/ on main before Forge can run it, and Forge cannot consume a .zip pack at all (forge/src/ui/app.mjs:190), which is a wider gap than the device path alone. Commit-first means every Forge run is tied to a committed artefact - and that IS ruling-supported, contrary to the earlier draft of this row: RUL-2026-09-12-001 (ACTIVE) wants content 'authored, compiled and validated through the repository's canonical scripts from the Forge interface without requiring routine chat/agent/file relay between design and build' (824c4d58:docs/RULINGS.md:148), and RUL-2026-09-12-002 makes the repository the owner of durable facts and generated build artifacts, with repository operations as approved typed operations (824c4d58:docs/RULINGS.md:163). Both rulings point away from restoring a device-file relay, not toward it. Authority caveat: neither ruling is on the working checkout's main (docs/RULINGS.md is 137 lines and ends at RUL-2026-09-08-007); they live on chatgpt/forge-quest-studio-foundation@824c4d58, which this planning pass has consumed (docs/forge_next/00_CONTEXT.md:10; K_USER_DECISIONS.md:14). Archiving interaction: push/README.md:3-4 requires archiving spent manifests, and the archive is archive/spent-manifests/ at repo ROOT (push/archive does not exist). Archiving an in-flight manifest breaks resume for that job - but only once the runner's in-memory copy is gone, because app.mjs:252 guards the refetch; within one page session resume still works. Inferred (no committed capture of a 404 resume). Documentation drift: push/README.md:4 still states 'Builder pickers list .json and .zip files from push/', true of Builder (builder_bundle.js:836-841) and false of Forge.
rows.used_in_real_work: no - Builder runs are provably untraceable to an ingress path, so no committed artefact shows a device/paste run. All 42 bundles in harvests/inbox/ were parsed: the 35 Builder bundles stamp only {builder: BVER, cfg: CFG.state='generated'} with no manifest-identity field (builder_bundle.js:764), while all 7 Forge bundles carry journal.manifestPath pointing into push/ (00_forge_readonly_smoke, 01_old_ghost_format_capture, 02_one_perfect_crop_asset_probe, 03_tnr_art_style_reference_capture, 04_one_perfect_crop_bandit_ai_probe x3). pipeline.md:310 and builder_bundle.js:150 record why the Load button exists, and push/ plus archive/spent-manifests/ hold both .json manifests and .zip packs, so the pack path was certainly exercised at some point - but 'a run used the device loader rather than the repo picker' is unevidenced in either direction. Behaviour-proven for the non-recording; Inferred for pack use.
rows.retirement_blocker: conditional - and the condition is narrower than 'restore the Load button'. It blocks retirement only if operators need to run work that is not yet committed to push/ (offline or fast-iteration), and any replacement must satisfy the no-routine-file-relay bar of RUL-2026-09-12-001 rather than re-adding a device relay. It is not a safety function; the safer reading is that commit-first is the intended end state. The real open item is already framed as K-39 'Artifact promotion gate and the journaled Studio to runner contract' (docs/forge_next/K_USER_DECISIONS.md:405-420, OPEN, Fable with director approval), whose advisory recommendation (a) is to promote into push/ at an explicit package gate, 'keeping one runner ingress'. Secondary, separable sub-gap: Forge has no .zip pack reader anywhere, which also lands on P-06. Gate: G-10 (retirement ruling and loader decommission).
rows.proposed_disposition: needs-user-decision - but bound to the existing K-39 / G-10 frame, not an open-ended question. Ask: does the operator need a Forge-internal ingress for uncommitted work, and if so is it (a) Studio-to-push/ promotion at a package gate through pushpack.py (K-39 recommendation; keeps one ingress and a repository history of what was run) or (b) a device import that preflight, parseManifest, planOrder and the auth gate must additionally cover? Re-adding Builder's raw textarea/device loader verbatim is the option least compatible with RUL-2026-09-12-001/002. No game-source procedure is touched by this capability (ingress is entirely client-side), so any chosen option is implementable with zero game change; the matrix has no zero_game_change_feasible column (B_PARITY_MATRIX.md:59-60,109-110) so none was added.

rows.builder_behavior: ⇩ Repo picker: prompt for a directory (default push), then a prompt accepting a number, list ('1,3'), range ('2-4') or 'all' over the .json/.zip listing sorted by numeric filename prefix (:824,:829-830). A SINGLE pick does not build at all - it only loads the file into the textarea and returns (:856-859). At >=2 picks one confirm ('▶ Build N manifests in listed order? This is ONE write batch; each file commits its own results bundle.', :860) is followed by a sequential per-file loop (:862-870): zip -> loadPack, json -> parse() (parse failure is caught, loadPack outcome is NOT checked), then await build(), then a per-file verdict computed as rows.filter(state==='error') and a '✓/⚠/✗' line, ending in a 'batch done: ' summary (:868-871). idmap, filemap, rows and MANIFEST are module-level and are never reset between files (:552). The same repoPick also drives a second multi-select loop on the 👁 Reads button, with no confirm, a get*/list* allowlist refusal, and an UNCONDITIONAL '✓' per file (:873-886). What shipped diverges from WO-06's spec: no checklist UI, numeric filename order rather than topological cross-ref order, per-FILE rather than per-ENTRY isolation, and resume by idmap create-skip rather than an in-session resume (docs/PLAN_2026-08-30_stack_optimization.md:159-162 vs the code).
rows.forge_behavior: NOT SUPPORTED, and nothing approximates it. The picker renders one tap-target per file, each calling selectManifest(entry) on a single entry which overwrites state.selected (screens.mjs:84; app.mjs:209-225); startJob reads that single selection (app.mjs:228-244); App._drive refuses a second run while one is in flight ('a job is already running', app.mjs:264-266, cleared in finally at :297); Journal.open refuses a second non-terminal job for the same manifestHash and tells the operator to resume instead (journal.mjs:237-246, test-proven at test/adversarial.test.mjs:115-116). Each manifest is therefore its own job, bundle and export cycle. Forge CAN hold several open jobs at once - journal.resumable() feeds a list on the home screen (screens.mjs:13,24) - but each is started and resumed by its own tap. grep over forge/src finds no manifest-level batch or queue; the only 'batch' in Forge is tRPC request batching in transport/budget.
rows.safety_compat_notes: The Builder's batch summary is not trustworthy and its 'each file commits its own results bundle' promise is not kept. The per-file verdict is rows.filter(state==='error') (:868), but at least four hard-failure paths inside build() return early without marking any row error - the L17 @img-without-imgSizes guard explicitly resets every row to 'pending' (:723), the v4.32 unresolved-pool-code guard returns bare (:741), and the missing-image and upload-failure paths return bare (:743) - and the bundle is only assembled after the write loop (:764). A batched file that wrote nothing therefore prints '✓ name' AND emits no bundle; the ❌ text it wrote to the status line is overwritten by the next file's line and then by 'batch done'. Ironic case: the v4.32 guard exists precisely to stop 'an empty kit and a green row' (:1-6) and in a batch it produces a green row. The zip branch never checks loadPack's outcome (:865); loadPack swallows its integrity failure (:508) and every other throw (:512), and on the generic catch the previous file's rows/MANIFEST survive (:552), so build() re-runs and exports the PREVIOUS manifest under the current file's name. filemap is merged and never cleared (:504,:890) and the image picker falls back to a by-BYTE-SIZE match across the whole accumulated filemap (:743), so a later file can silently upload an earlier zip's byte-identical image. The 👁 Reads loop is worse: '✓' unconditionally (:884). Forge's single-job invariant (app.mjs:265) plus per-manifest journals (journal.mjs:237-246) avoid all of this by construction. If a Forge queue is ever built it must be a queue of independent jobs - fresh idmap/filemap scope per manifest, one journal and one bundle per manifest, a stop-on-first-failure default, and a summary derived from jobOutcome(job) rather than from a leftover global - and must NOT reproduce the Builder's semantics.
rows.used_in_real_work: unprovable from the committed record, and the record cannot settle it either way: no builder results bundle carries a manifest path or batch marker (bundle keys are builder,at,checks,cfg,postflight,entries,captures,idmap - builder_bundle.js:764, and all 34 builder bundles in harvests/inbox). WO-06's own acceptance evidence ('induced-failure batch isolates + resumes', docs/PLAN_2026-08-30_stack_optimization.md:168-172,310) is not present in the repository either.

(1) PROCEDURES is a frozen table of exactly 43 audited paths (routers ai, bloodline, gameAsset, item, jutsu, profile, quests) carrying kind/limited/mcp/auth; procedure(path) throws 'unknown procedure' and TrpcClient.batch calls it for every element before any fetch. There is no `select` equivalent. Closing P-10 needs four things, not one: (i) registry rows for combat.getBattleHistory / combat.getBattleEntries / gameAsset.getAllFolders, transcribed from the pinned source per procedures.mjs:1-22 (all three verified at 345d18ac: combat.ts:382 and :530 protected, asset.ts:83 public/limited); (ii) a capture read path that passes the manifest's input through instead of rebuilding {id} (reader.mjs:13-16) - without it the two combat procedures remain uncallable even once registered; (iii) support for paged/filtered list captures, which also unblocks the already-registered gameAsset.getAll and quests.getAll (reader.mjs:76) - a pure Forge-side fix needing no registry change and no source re-audit; (iv) a decision on bodies, because the deliverable of push/05 and push/06 IS the response body and Forge's summary mode keeps none (runner.mjs:589) while persist:'full' is capped at 7 point reads with a required input.id (manifest.mjs:131-137, captures.mjs:58-66). rows.forge_behavior: Manifest load accepts ANY proc string for a capture (only persist:'full' is gated to the audited point-read allowlist), so a getAll capture validates. At run time Runner._captures takes c.id first, falling back to input.id ?? input.userId (the manifest normalizer derives that same id from input); a non-null id routes to reader.get, otherwise to reader.list. reader.list hard-refuses any path not matching /\.getAll(Ai)?Names$/ with a plain Error ('needs a paged input'), and for the paths it does accept always sends input undefined, which the envelope transmits explicitly as {"json":null,"meta":{"values":["undefined"]}}. Consequences: (a) a getAll capture is not merely unsupported - the thrown Error is not Paused/AuthRefused/RateLimited/transport, so run() releases the lease and rethrows, _drive catches it as a generic run failure, and NO results bundle is exported (export is gated on DONE/INCOMPLETE), leaving the job non-terminal; capture.before precedes every item, so a mixed manifest aborts before its first write. (b) The five input-less name lists work correctly (Behaviour-proven by a Forge 0.2.1 bundle). (c) gameAsset.getAllNames - the only name list that takes an input - is sent undefined against a REQUIRED z.object, so it is rejected rather than 'running unfiltered'; the same defective call sits on the asset entity's dedupNames and orphan-reconciler path (recipes.mjs:29 -> runner.mjs:542, reconciler.mjs:72,106), and the test fake ignores input on getAllNames so no Forge test can catch it. The journal entry records the manifest's input as written and carries no scope sentence.

rows.forge_behavior: Forge is narrower on three independent axes. (a) Reachability: a capture path must be one of the 43 rows of the generated audited registry, or procedure() throws 'unknown procedure' and _requireAuth rethrows it, so combat.* cannot be read at all; and a capture with no id goes to CachedReader.list(), which refuses any path not matching /\.getAll(Ai)?Names$/, so paged getAll dumps cannot be read either. (b) Input fidelity: for a point read the manifest's `input` is used only to derive an id and to journal; the request actually sent is readInput(path,id) = {id} (or {userId} for profile.getAi), so arbitrary query inputs are dropped, and `select` is parsed away entirely by normalizeCapture. (c) Persistence: default persist 'summary' journals only {phase, proc, input, ok, rows, error} - no status, at, select or scope; persist 'full' is allowed only for FULL_PERSIST_PATHS (gameAsset.get, jutsu.get, item.get, bloodline.get, quests.get, profile.getAi, ai.getAiProfile) with an input id, body <= 512 KiB (over it is an explicit failure, never truncation), stored once in IndexedDB capture_snapshots and attached at export. List and name-list bodies land in the read cache but can never be exported.

rows.safety_compat_notes: select is what keeps large research reads (battle history, 1,490-row name lists) small enough to commit - Builder's own schema comment says so; it is the projection K-06/R-04 would need anyway to commit anything from a protected read. scope is an evidence-honesty annotation about filtered lists, and it is provably decorative: harvest.py ignores it for Builder bundles too and regenerates the same warning from `input`, so losing it costs a sentence in the raw bundle, not a capability. The real migration hazard is not the absence but the silence: Forge drops `select` with no warning while validating `persist` strictly, and the content skill still ships a capture example that uses select - so a migrated manifest degrades invisibly. Minimum fix regardless of disposition: reject or warn on unknown capture keys. Any future projected mode must keep rows counted pre-trim (Builder does) or the absence evidence is lost. Zero game change either way: both features only shape the local bundle - no extra request, no game write; the only new risk is what reaches the public repo.

Across jobs there is no srcId reuse: plan() opens a job and _create always sends when the item is op=create and state=PLANNED - idmap is read only by planOrder/_lookup for @ref resolution, never as a 'does this srcId already exist' check. Journal.open refuses a duplicate manifestHash only while the earlier job is resumable (PAUSED, INCOMPLETE, or RUNNING with a non-terminal item); DONE and ABORTED jobs never block, and the jobId is minted fresh from Date.now(), so re-running a finished manifest re-creates every create and _remember overwrites idmap[srcId] with the duplicate's id - silently rebinding every later manifest's @ref to the duplicate. Warnings: the 'ran' pill in the picker (keyed on manifestPath across all journal jobs) and the start confirm, which names the create count ('N items (M creates)? This writes to the game.') but never says the manifest ran before. Both are weak: the pill disappears once 'Delete finished jobs' removes DONE/ABORTED jobs (which also drops those entityIds from journal.knownEntityIds, the set the reconciler uses to refuse cross-job adoption), and skip/adopt are rendered only on the OrphanCard, so there is no pre-run way to skip a create that already landed. No Forge test covers a re-run after DONE; the only duplicate-manifest test asserts the resumable case.

rows.safety_compat_notes: Recovery AND hygiene function, and the hygiene half is shared: Forge depends on the very map only the Builder can clear. Poisoning mechanism: the Builder's row key is j.srcId (562), so a create without srcId writes and later reads idmap[undefined] === idmap['undefined'] - 41 of the 42 committed results bundles carry 'undefined' -> 0QixZN9jD_bqAKTimDafB, and all 7 Forge bundles (entries 0) inherit the same 80-key poisoned map, so the coupling is behaviour-proven, not theoretical. Forge is immune to creating the defect (_remember guards falsy srcId; Forge never consults the idmap for create reuse - see P-21) but is exposed to consuming it through @ref/@img resolution, and it has no eviction path: import is merge-only in the Builder and absent in Forge, so retiring the Builder removes the only tool that can clear or repair the map both bundles share. A Reset is also coarse: it wipes the @img URL cache with the srcId map (176-181, 509-510), which is itself an argument for a per-key editor rather than a straight port of ⌫ Reset. Forge's cross-job protections (P-41) and journal-first idempotency reduce but do not replace import/reset.
